CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old female presenting with left shoulder pain that began one week ago. Patient reports the pain started during a gymnastics class when she may have fallen into a weird position or overextended during a move. Pain is constant with any kind of movement of the left shoulder. Patient self-treated with Tylenol for two or three days without relief. X-ray obtained shows no fracture or broken bone, suggesting joint injury. Patient reports past surgery on left arm but states doctor does not believe it is related to current pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Prior surgery on left arm.

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol (used for two to three days, ineffective).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient participates in gymnastics class.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Patient demonstrates pain with shoulder movement in multiple directions, including upward movement and backward movement. Any movement of the left shoulder elicits pain.

RESULTS
X-ray of left shoulder: No fracture or broken bone noted.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left shoulder joint injury. Recommend ibuprofen 600 mg three times daily for one week. Apply ice or heat pad as needed for pain relief. Rest left arm and avoid heavy lifting for three to four weeks; use right hand instead. Follow-up appointment in three weeks to reassess pain. If pain persists after three weeks, consider repeat x-ray at that time. Patient to call if pain worsens or if she wishes to schedule earlier follow-up appointment.
